classification.habitat: Open deciduous forests and cultivated areas of tropical and subtropical regions
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in the Indian subcontinent and South/Southeast Asia

identification.description: A deciduous tree with a comparatively straight trunk, broad opposite leaves and yellowish flowers; the ripe fruit becomes yellow to orange-yellow.
identification.whole_plant: Medium-sized deciduous tree with a spreading crown.
identification.root: Woody root system; medicinal root material should be authenticated against the correct species.
identification.stem: Young branches are relatively soft and greyish; mature trunk develops grey-brown bark.
identification.leaf: Large, simple, opposite leaves; broadly ovate to cordate and often unequal at the base.
identification.flower: Flowers occur in terminal or axillary branched clusters and are yellowish with darker markings.
identification.fruit: Fleshy drupe, green when immature and yellow to orange-yellow on ripening, usually containing a hard stone.
identification.seed: Seed is enclosed within the hard stone of the drupe.
identification.bark: Outer bark grey to grey-brown; inner bark is fibrous and should be compared with authenticated pharmacopoeial material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Gmelina arborea is a recognized medicinal and timber tree. Its Ayurvedic identity and therapeutic discussion should be kept distinct from modern clinical efficacy claims.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated raw drug material; do not infer a clinical dose from this educational dossier.
